tcmvNext.label: expected October 2026
tcmvNext.note: Traficom (23 Jun 2026) and Reuters (6 Aug 2026) expect a vote in October. Trade press and trackers name 6 October 2026. Not on a published Commission TCMV agenda as of 2026-08-27.

sourcesNote: Statuses from official notices. Sweden row updated 1 September 2026 from Riksdag written answer 2025/26:1000. Tracker is a third-party view, not scraped live by this site.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.blurb: Provisional EU type-approval under Article 39, valid in the Netherlands. First in Europe. HW4 / AI4 only. Subscribe in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.authority: Ministry of Transport and Communications + LTSA
countries.blurb: National recognition of the Dutch provisional approval under Article 39(5).

countries.name: Estonia
countries.blurb: Recognises the Dutch type-approval. Official page: SAE Level 2; driver fully responsible.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.blurb: Accepts the Dutch provisional approval after its own document review. States the six-month lapse rule in public.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.blurb: Annick De Ridder (Flemish Minister of Mobility) signed recognition of the Dutch Article 39 file on 10 June 2026. Reporting, including VRT, says a regional type-approval signature has nationwide effect. Driver remains responsible. Not EU-wide TCMV approval.

countries.name: Germany
countries.blurb: KBA is assessing the Article 39 file. A test car was expected in July. No national go-ahead. Write for a TCMV yes.

countries.name: France
countries.blurb: Tabarot declined national recognition of the current product on 22 July 2026 and wants an EU-wide framework. Not a pending rubber-stamp.

countries.name: Italy
countries.authority: Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti (DG Motorizzazione)
countries.blurb: Tesla has filed for recognition of the Dutch homologation. MIT says it is in analysis (reported July 2026). No customer activation. Day of filing not published.

countries.name: Spain
countries.authority: Ministerio de Industria y Turismo + DGT
countries.blurb: Reported 23 July 2026: Minister Hereu said Spain would not unilaterally adopt the Dutch file and is coordinating with the Commission, DGT and UN. A DGT test fleet is not customer approval. The ministerial reply was not found on mintur.gob.es.

countries.name: Poland
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public Article 39(5) position and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Romania
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public position.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.blurb: No customer approval. Trafikverket’s 30 April TCMV letter recommends a no unless Speed Offset is removed. Infrastrukturminister Carlson’s written answer (letter 31 August, published 1 September 2026) restates a union-wide ADAS ambition and still takes Trafikverket into account. That is not a locked TCMV yes.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public Article 39(5) decision and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Greece
countries.blurb: Ministry said it would bring forward a bill to recognise the Dutch approval. No confirmation the bill was enacted. Do not treat Greece as approved.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Austria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Finland
countries.blurb: Official assessment underway (takeover time, Finnish highways, Speed Offset, vehicle ageing). Traficom says it could recognise before the EU vote if extra information arrives; it has not.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no. Left-hand traffic is an extra technical issue.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.blurb: Baltic rumours of an imminent sign-off were not matched by a published decision as of 27 August 2026.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Malta
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.blurb: Cannot use Article 39(5). Separate GB type-approval. R171 Series 02 is the realistic UN path. Not approved.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.blurb: Applies R171 as a 1958 party; cannot accept the Dutch Article 39 file. Ride-alongs are not an approval.

countries.name: Norway
countries.blurb: EEA, not Article 39. Has raised Speed Offset and winter-road concerns. Testing is not approval.
